about: The numbers of Examples 10.3.4 and 10.3.6 of the post "Features", keyed by the post's placeholders. Each: value, text (what to print), how (how it was computed). Written by gptpp.export.dictionary_numbers from the lab's records; blocks are counted from 1 in text.

width of pico's dictionary.how: the dictionary of pico that the figures read (sparsity-against-fidelity.json, pico, used)

block of pico that its dictionary reads.how: the residual stream after this block, counted from 1 (resid_post.2 in the lab's names)

block of gpt-pp that the dictionaries re.how: the residual stream after this block, counted from 1 (resid_post.7 in the lab's names)

dictionary widths trained on gpt-pp.how: the widths n of the TopK dictionaries in the folder of gpt-pp's dictionaries

values of k trained on gpt-pp.how: the values of k of those dictionaries; every width was trained at every k

training vectors per gpt-pp dictionary.how: activation vectors (one a token) each dictionary was trained on, drawn from random windows of the training text; the same stream for every dictionary

other kinds of dictionary trained, and t.text: 4 ReLU autoencoders with an L1 penalty (the architecture of Definition 10.2.2 with the decoder norm in the penalty), n = 8,192, at penalties that leave between 14 and 86 latents active a token
other kinds of dictionary trained, and t.how: the ReLU dictionaries in the same folder, trained on the same activations for the same number of steps

its width.how: the dictionary of gpt-pp that the figures read (sparsity-against-fidelity.json, gpt-pp, used)

random latents examined.how: the random list of the feature browser: a seeded draw from all latents of the dictionary, nobody chose them

random latents that could be given one l.how: One reader (the builder of the figure, a language model) read, for each of the 60 latents of the browser's random list, its three strongest examples, two sampled firings between a quarter and a half of its peak, two below a quarter, its five most frequent tokens and the five tokens its direction raises most. A latent counts as 'one' if one short description (a word in a context, a role in the sentence, a kind of word, a piece of a word, a place in the text) fits the strongest examples and the samples above a quarter of the peak; stray firings below a quarter of the peak were tolerated. Otherwise 'mixed'. One pass, no second reader, no score of agreement.

mean absolute cosine between its decoder.how: the mean of |u_i . u_j| over all pairs of different latents of the dictionary (n = 16384, d = 768); two random directions in 768 dimensions have sqrt(2 / (pi d)) = 0.029

median cosine to the nearest neighbor.how: for each latent the largest cosine u_i . u_j with another latent of the same dictionary; the median over latents

held-out tokens used for evaluation.how: held-out tokens whose activations were read: every token of the held-out split except the document-start marks and the first 16 tokens of each window; the loss is measured on the first 1,030,157 of them

its normalized error.how: sum |x - x^|^2 / sum |x - mean|^2 over those tokens, the mean being theirs (Definition 10.3.3)

its loss recovered.how: (H0 - H*) / (H0 - H) with the stream replaced by zero for H0 = 10.89 nats; against the dataset mean instead of zero (8.29 nats) it is 96.8%

gpt-pp's cross-entropy, nats per token.how: gpt-pp's next-token loss on the same held-out windows, on the targets that follow the tokens read

the same with the reconstruction spliced.how: the same loss when the stream after the block is replaced by the dictionary's reconstruction at every token read

share of its latents that are dead.how: latents that are active on none of the 9.8 million held-out tokens (the post's definition says 10^7: the held-out split is smaller)

index of the steered latent.how: the default feature of the steering figure; its index in pico's dictionary

what the steered latent fires on.how: its four most frequent tokens on held-out text, most frequent first (the feature browser shows them with their shares); the figure calls the latent "river, pond, lake"

clamp multiple.how: the latent is held at 3.74 = this multiple of its largest activation on held-out text (7.49), at every token after the document-start mark, as in (10.10)

stories sampled per condition.how: stories of at most 72 tokens continued from "Once upon a time," at temperature 0.7, seeds 0 to 299; the same seeds with and without the clamp; computed on the 8-bit weights that the page runs, not on the checkpoint

word or theme counted in the stories.how: a story counts if a word of the list begins a word of it (so "rivers" counts for "river"); the list was fixed before sampling

share of clamped stories with it.how: the share of the clamped stories that count

share of unclamped stories with it.how: the share of the stories written without the clamp, from the same opening on the same seeds, that count

pico's held-out loss with the clamp.how: pico's next-token loss on 1024 held-out windows of 256 tokens with the latent clamped at every token read; computed on the 8-bit weights that the page runs, not on the checkpoint

pico's held-out loss, nats per token.how: the same loss without the clamp, on the same windows; computed on the 8-bit weights that the page runs, not on the checkpoint (the checkpoint itself: see `also`)

a second training run.how: for each latent of the dictionary the figures use, the largest cosine between its decoder direction and any decoder direction of a second dictionary trained the same way on the same model and layer with another seed (other initial directions, other random windows of the same training text)

differences from the post's definitions: Definition 10.3.2 writes TopK as TopK_k(W_enc (x - b_dec)). The lab's dictionaries are TopK_k(ReLU(W_enc (x - b_dec) + b_enc)): an encoder bias, and a ReLU before the k largest are kept, as in the released code of the TopK paper and in the dictionary_learning library. With the ReLU a token has at most k active latents, not exactly k (the measured L0 is within 0.01 of k), and no activation is negative, which Definition 10.2.1 requires.

Definition 10.3.3 calls a latent dead if it is active on none of 10^7 tokens. The lab counts over the held-out tokens read (see `eval_tokens` by model): about 9.8 million for gpt-pp and 5.1 million for pico, whose held-out split is smaller.

The dictionary reads activations with the dataset mean subtracted and scaled by one constant (mean norm sqrt(d)); activations f_i and the clamp value c are in those units, and the direction u_i of (10.10) is the unit decoder row divided by that constant. The document-start mark and the first 16 tokens of every window are neither read nor replaced.

Definition 10.2.2, (10.7): the lab's ReLU dictionaries with an L1 penalty are the form of April 2024, not the form of 2023: the penalty is lambda sum_i f_i |u_i| with the decoder rows left free (no unit-norm constraint; the norms are folded into the encoder after training), the squared error is measured on the normalized activations, lambda is warmed up over the first twentieth of training, and no latent is resampled.

Example 10.3.6 says the latent is clamped at a multiple of its largest activation; the multiple measured is 0.5, half its largest activation. At one times the largest activation the stories are no longer readable (see `clamp`), and Remark 10.3.7's ten times is the 2024 paper's setting, not this one.
